key_findings: FR-043 IS PARTIALLY REFUTED BY LCM REALITY (most valuable finding of the spurt, and the worked justification for D-00). HCParser.Update() is itself conditional -- 'if (m_changeListener.Reset() || m_forceUpdate) LoadParser();' -- so Reload()->Update() as specced does NOT unconditionally discard. FieldWorks' own force-reload path is ParserWorker.ReloadGrammarAndLexicon(): Reset() THEN CheckNeedsUpdate(). Bound wrong, it fails SILENTLY and serves the next parse from the stale grammar the caller believes it discarded.

Reset() and IsUpToDate() are MISSING from parser_probe.py's HCPARSER_MEMBERS, but FR-041/SC-016 forbid touching that file. Resolved by D-02: each check probes what its own surface binds -- the requirement lands on the NEW flexicon-side probe, parser_probe.py stays untouched, SC-016 stays green. Consequence: the two member lists diverge in BOTH directions after CP2, so the spec's 'this repository keeps its larger check' becomes false and must read 'different, overlapping' (spec edit E3).

THERE IS NO JOB/QUEUE/WORKER/RUN-RECORD MACHINERY ANYWHERE in this repo. SessionState is in-memory; run_script_async is one create_subprocess_exec + wait_for with no handle and no cancellation token; the only concurrency primitive on the request path is kernel.project_write_locks (per-project asyncio.Lock). US4 extends NOTHING -- 100% net-new. Best structural precedent for the run record is skeleton_storage.py:43-50 (JSONL append under a threading.Lock + env dir override).

The Verbatim Constraint index path 'index/python/flexicon_api_v4.9.0.json' DOES NOT EXIST. Real root is src/flextoolsmcp/index/python/. Worse: the sibling flexicon_lcm_bridge_v<ver>.json is version-locked to the same flexicon version (server.py:665 loads it keyed to self.flexicon_version, handlers/equivalence.py:64 consumes it) and the spec never mentions it -- shipping only the api file SILENTLY removes the bridge for 4.9.0. refresh.py:217 derives the bridge prefix, so a full refresh produces both; the risk is a hand-copied index.

FR-017's no-XCore guarantee rests on .NET LAZY PER-TYPE BINDING, not on absence of a reference: ParserCore.csproj DOES reference xCore/xCoreInterfaces/FwUtils at assembly level; the 'using XCore;' statements are confined to ParseFiler/ParserScheduler/ParserWorker, not HCParser/HCLoader/IParser.
